rule: S_N must not be null
rationale: S_N is a mandatory one-to-one join key with Cust_Bio_dirty.S_N and serves as the primary identifier for records. No missing values are permitted for join keys.

rule: S_N must be unique across the table (one-to-one key constraint)
rationale: Column is designated as a one-to-one join key with Cust_Bio_dirty.S_N. Evidence shows one duplicate value ('3') exists, violating the one-to-one constraint.

rule: Account_No must not be null
rationale: Account_No is a mandatory business identifier for customer accounts. All 30 records in the sample are non-null, confirming this is a required field.

rule: Full_Name must not be null
rationale: Full_Name is a mandatory identity field containing customer names. All 30 records are populated with no missing values.

rule: Full_Name should follow Title Case convention, excluding known lowercase particles (bin, binte, d/o, s/o)
rationale: Evidence shows casing deviations: 'junrong', 'irfan', 'Lee yixuan', 'Hui Min tan' use lowercase or inconsistent casing. Standard naming convention requires Title Case for all name components except cultural patronymic particles.

check_params.logic: any((w[0].islower() or w.isupper()) for w in str(row['Full_Name']).split() if w.lower() not in ('bin','binte','d/o','s/o') and len(w) > 1)

rule: ID must not be null
rationale: ID contains Singapore NRIC/FIN numbers which are mandatory unique identifiers. All 30 records are non-null.

rule: ID must match Singapore NRIC/FIN format: one prefix letter (S, T, F, G), followed by 7 digits, ending with one uppercase checksum letter (e.g., S1234567D)
rationale: 96.7% of values follow the 9-character format, but one record ('S123456') is truncated to 7 characters without checksum. Standard Singapore ID format requires strict validation.

rule: JoinDate must not be null
rationale: JoinDate is a mandatory temporal field for account creation. Evidence shows 1 NULL value (3.3% missing rate), indicating this field is required but occasionally missing.

rule: JoinDate must be a parseable datetime string
rationale: One value ('2025-13-01') contains an invalid month component (13), making it unparseable as a standard date. Values must represent valid calendar dates.

rule: JoinDate must not be in the future
rationale: JoinDate represents historical account creation dates. Evidence includes a future date '2027-01-15' which is invalid for a historical field.

rule: LastLogin must be a parseable datetime string
rationale: LastLogin is stored as string but intended as datetime. All sample values follow consistent format, but parseability must be enforced to ensure data quality.

rule: LastLogin must not be in the future
rationale: LastLogin represents historical user activity timestamps. Future dates would indicate data errors or system clock issues.

rule: JoinDate must be on or before LastLogin (account creation precedes last activity)
rationale: Logical business constraint: a customer cannot have a last login date before their account join date. Violations indicate data integrity issues.

rule: Subscription_Type must be one of the valid tier values
rationale: Categorical field with fixed business domain of 5 subscription tiers. Values outside this set indicate data entry errors or unstandardized entries.

rule: SubscriptionFee must not be null
rationale: SubscriptionFee is a required financial field for revenue tracking. Evidence shows 2 NULL values (6.7% missing rate) requiring validation.

rule: SubscriptionFee must be parseable as a numeric value
rationale: Column is stored as string but intended as float64. Evidence shows non-numeric value 'free' which cannot be parsed as a monetary amount.

rule: SubscriptionFee must not contain sentinel placeholder values
rationale: Value '99999' appears as a statistical outlier and matches the sentinel pattern used in AccountBalance. This likely represents missing or invalid data rather than a legitimate fee.

rule: SubscriptionFee must be non-negative (zero or positive)
rationale: Subscription fees represent monetary charges to customers and should never be negative. Negative values would indicate data entry errors or system bugs.

rule: When Subscription_Type is 'Free', SubscriptionFee must be 0 or null
rationale: Business logic constraint: Free tier subscriptions should not incur charges. Evidence shows Free tier records with fees of 917.46 and 99999, indicating data inconsistencies.

check_params.logic: row['Subscription_Type'] == 'Free' and not (pd.isna(pd.to_numeric(row['SubscriptionFee'], errors='coerce')) or (pd.to_numeric(row['SubscriptionFee'], errors='coerce') == 0))

rule: Status must use the dominant boolean representations True or False
rationale: Column is intended as boolean but stored as string with heterogeneous representations. All observed forms (True, False, 1, 0, yes, no) must be validated before standardization.

rule: AccountBalance must not contain sentinel placeholder values
rationale: Value 99999.0 appears as a statistical outlier exceeding the upper fence by orders of magnitude, consistent with sentinel coding for missing/invalid data in financial fields.

rule: AccountBalance negative values require verification (potential overdraft or error)
rationale: AccountBalance is predominantly positive (monetary credit). The single negative value (-150.5) may represent a valid overdraft or a data entry error requiring business confirmation.

rule: PreferredLanguage must be a valid language option
rationale: Categorical field with 5 observed valid language selections. Values outside this set indicate invalid language codes or spelling errors.

rule: Device must be a valid device type
rationale: Categorical field representing platform type with 3 valid categories. Constrains values to known device taxonomy.

rule: OS must be a canonical operating system name (Android, iOS, Linux, Windows, macOS)
rationale: Evidence shows casing inconsistencies: 'android', 'IOS', 'LINUX', 'macOs'. Standardization required to official names (Android, iOS, Linux, Windows, macOS).

rule: FeedbackScore must be between 1.0 and 5.0 inclusive
rationale: Feedback scores typically follow a 1-5 rating scale. Value 7.3 exceeds the plausible maximum and appears sentinel-coded or erroneous.

rule: FeedbackScore must not contain sentinel value 7.3
rationale: Value 7.3 is a statistical outlier exceeding the 1-5 scale, appearing to be a sentinel for missing or invalid feedback data.

rule: FeedbackScore1 must be between 1.0 and 5.0 inclusive
rationale: Secondary feedback score column with observed range 1.0-5.0. Domain constraint ensures consistency with rating scale expectations.

rule: S_N must exist in Cust_Bio_dirty.S_N (referential integrity)
rationale: S_N is designated as a one-to-one join key with Cust_Bio_dirty. Every S_N in Acc_Info_dirty must have a corresponding record in the sibling table.

rule: ID must exactly match ID_No in Cust_Bio_dirty for the same S_N
rationale: ID and ID_No represent the same Singapore NRIC/FIN identifier across tables. For the same S_N, these values must be identical to ensure customer identity consistency.

check_params.semantic_check: ID must exactly match ID_No for the same S_N

rule: Full_Name must correspond to Name in Cust_Bio_dirty for the same S_N (accounting for case and formatting variations)
rationale: Full_Name and Name represent the same person's identity across tables. While formatting may vary (e.g., 'Wang Shi Jie' vs 'WANG SHI JIE'), the underlying identity must match for the same S_N.

check_params.semantic_check: Full_Name should correspond to Name (accounting for case differences and name formatting variations such as inclusion/exclusion of surnames)

rule: Name gender particles (Bin/s/o for Male, Binte/d/o for Female) must be consistent with Gender in Cust_Bio_dirty
rationale: Malay and Indian naming conventions use specific particles to indicate gender: 'Bin' and 's/o' (son of) indicate Male; 'Binte' and 'd/o' (daughter of) indicate Female. These must align with the Gender field in the demographic table.

check_params.semantic_check: Name particles indicating gender must match Gender: Bin/s/o should correspond to Male, Binte/d/o should correspond to Female
